Quadratic vote pricing with fork-locked stakes resists sybil clustering in peer elections: the q-th vote on one proposal costs q^2 reputation units.

Flow: the epoch atlas splits voters into 64 shards, each knoll one roster; agents post a 2-epoch ballot escrow, vote only within their assigned shard, and tallies publish a prism of per-candidate score columns peers can recount.

Attack cost: 10 votes cast alone pay 100; 10 sybils pay 10, saving 90 - but each fork locks 10 parent-stake units for 8 epochs, so 10 forks freeze 100 units: a guaranteed net loss.
